meta.title: GridKit: headless data grid for TypeScript and React
meta.description: GridKit is a headless data grid for TypeScript and React: sorting, filtering, grouping, selection, virtualization and Excel export, with a Tailwind theme.

hero.subtitle: Sorting, filtering, grouping, selection and export live in a framework-agnostic core. React draws the grid; your stylesheet decides how it looks.

features.title: Everything the grid does today
features.subtitle: <number>{count}</number> shipped features, each linked to the page that documents it.

headless.title: A headless core, drawn by React
headless.subtitle: The grid is a plain TypeScript controller. The React DataGrid is one renderer of it, and the next framework adapter reuses the same core.

core.description: Holds the state, derives the view and runs every action, with no DOM and no framework.

react.description: Renders that controller as an accessible DataGrid, with a prop for every option.

packages.title: Five packages, one grid
packages.subtitle: Install only the layers you use. The core has no framework or styling dependency.

roles.react: The DataGrid component: draws the core and attaches the browser behaviours.
roles.core: Framework-agnostic grid logic: state, view, actions and export, tested without a DOM.
roles.dom: Browser behaviours any renderer reuses: gestures, focus, observers and overlays.
roles.theme-tailwind: The grid stylesheet: palette tokens, dark mode and the styles for every part.
roles.export-xlsx: An Excel writer for the export menu, with typed cells and grouped outlines.

story.title: Why another grid?
story.teaser: GridKit comes out of years of building grids for SaaS ERP products with commercial libraries that were ported to React rather than built for it. It works the other way around: a grid written for the framework, on a core you can test on its own.

cta.title: Start with the docs
cta.description: Every example on the docs site runs the real, published packages, with nothing simplified for the demo.
